cases.factual_findings: Acasti's Nasdaq-listed ACST security was common shares; later domestication evidence confirms the same outstanding common shares continued as common stock. The later GRCE name/ticker transition does not alter the decision-period legal type.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: Multiple CUSIPs reflect reverse splits, continuance/domestication and later corporate/name changes. Full identifier-chain perfection is unnecessary to determine the 2021 traded security's common-share legal type.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that the traded ACST/GRCE lineage during the canonical interval was preferred, partnership/unit, trust, warrant, right or other non-common instrument.

cases.factual_findings: Akanda stated that its AKAN common shares underwent a 1-for-4.5 reverse split effective April 13, 2026 and received CUSIP 00971M700. This directly covers the canonical interval.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The many CUSIPs are successive reverse-split identifiers for the same common-share class.
cases.contradiction_search: No contrary evidence that AKAN in the canonical interval represented a non-common instrument.

cases.factual_findings: Authoritative SEC evidence identifies CUSIP 60852L205 as MKDTY ADSs, each representing 45 Class A ordinary shares of the issuer.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP 60852L106/205 reflects ADS-program ratio/identifier changes; both concern depositary interests in Class A ordinary equity.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that MKDTY represented preferred shares or another non-common underlying class.

cases.factual_findings: Concordia Healthcare's publicly traded security was its common shares; SEC registration documents separately enumerate preferred shares, warrants and other instruments, confirming the common-share class is distinct.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIPs span Concordia renamings/reorganizations and later successor identifiers. Those identity events do not establish a legal-type change in the canonical interval.
cases.contradiction_search: Separate preferred/warrant classes existed as possible issuer securities, but no evidence shows the traded CXRXF lineage in this interval was one of those non-common classes.

cases.factual_findings: SEC-filed holdings data identifies ALLTEL Corp CUSIP 020039103 as common stock. The canonical interval ends immediately before the 2007 take-private closing.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP 016090102 is an identity-chain anomaly/successor association and is retained separately; it does not make the factual type of 020039103 ambiguous.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that the listed ALLTEL security represented preferred stock, units, warrants or rights.

cases.factual_findings: AnPac's listed ADSs each represented Class A ordinary shares. A separate 2020-21 preference-share financing existed, but the preference shares themselves were not the listed ADS class; the ADSs represented ordinary shares.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: 03635R107/206/305 reflect later ADS-ratio/name changes in the AnPac/Fresh2 program. The decision-period instrument under 03635R107 was an ADS on Class A ordinary equity.
cases.contradiction_search: The issuer's separate Class A preference shares were explicitly distinct from the listed ADSs; no evidence shows the canonical traded security was the preferred instrument.

cases.factual_findings: OceanFreight's Nasdaq-traded OCNF security was its common shares. The issuer also had subordinated shares, but those were a separate class and had converted to common shares by August 2008, before the canonical interval.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP changes are consistent with share adjustments; they do not indicate a switch from the traded common-share class to a non-common class.
cases.contradiction_search: The separate subordinated-share class was investigated and does not apply to the 2009 OCNF traded security.

cases.factual_findings: Big Tree Cloud states that after its February 2026 share consolidation and dual-class implementation, DSY continued trading as Class A Ordinary Shares under CUSIP G1263B132.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: Prior CUSIPs reflect pre-consolidation/reorganization identifiers. The canonical interval is directly covered by G1263B132 Class A ordinary shares.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that DSY during the interval was a preferred, unit, warrant, right or trust instrument.

cases.factual_findings: Nortel's public NNC security is repeatedly identified by the issuer as NNC common shares; later NRTLQ was the OTC symbol for those same common shares. Preferred shares are separately identified as NNL preferred shares.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The CUSIP set includes Nortel corporate/security identifiers beyond the exact public common-share chain. That identity noise does not make the legal type of the decision-period NNC common shares ambiguous.
cases.contradiction_search: Issuer filings explicitly distinguish NNC common shares from NNL preferred shares; the reviewed security is the common-share lineage.

cases.factual_findings: Orange's issuer filing states that its American Depositary Shares each represent one Ordinary Share. The earlier France Telecom CUSIP 35177Q105 is documented in SEC-filed holdings as a sponsored ADR, consistent with the same ordinary-share ADR program lineage.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The interval spans France Telecom-to-Orange naming and depositary/CUSIP changes. These are identity/program changes, not a legal-type change away from ADRs on ordinary equity.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that the ORAN/France Telecom ADR lineage represented preferred shares.

cases.factual_findings: SEC-filed security tables identify Visionary Holdings Inc CUSIP 92838F200 as common stock ('COM NEW'). The predecessor 92838F101 reflects the pre-adjustment identifier.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP 92838F101 to 92838F200 is an identifier/share-adjustment change in the common-stock lineage.
cases.contradiction_search: No authoritative evidence found that the traded Visionary security in the interval was a preferred share, unit, warrant or right.

cases.factual_findings: Later authoritative issuer evidence states the company has one Exchange Act-registered class, common shares, and traces the same corporate issuer through its later name change to MindWalk/HYFT.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The ticker/name and CUSIP sequence spans ImmunoPrecise/MindWalk identity changes. Later issuer evidence establishes that the equity class is common shares; no type transition is indicated.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence of a preferred, partnership/unit, trust, warrant or rights class replacing the traded common shares during the canonical interval.

cases.factual_findings: Psyence Biomedical states that PBM common shares continued trading after its January 2026 consolidation under new CUSIP 74449F407. This directly establishes common-share type within the canonical interval.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The CUSIPs reflect predecessor/reorganization and multiple consolidations. These are common-share identity adjustments.
cases.contradiction_search: The issuer separately references warrants and other equity instruments; the PBM listed security itself is expressly common shares.

cases.factual_findings: Antelope's AEHL security is expressly Class A Ordinary Shares. The March 2026 reverse split changed the CUSIP to G041JN148 while leaving the legal class as Class A ordinary shares.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The CUSIP history reflects predecessor names and repeated reverse splits; the canonical interval remains within the Class A ordinary-share lineage.
cases.contradiction_search: The issuer has Class B ordinary shares with different voting rights, but AEHL is the listed Class A ordinary-share class and remains common-equity under the contract.

cases.factual_findings: Core Scientific issuer filings identify CORZQ as common stock and separately identify CRZWQ as warrants exercisable for common stock. The canonical episode is the common-stock lineage.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP 739190106 reflects the predecessor Power & Digital Infrastructure Acquisition Corp identity before the de-SPAC; 21873J108 is Core Scientific common stock. The transition does not create non-common type ambiguity for the equity episode.
cases.contradiction_search: Warrants are explicitly a separate ticker/class and were not conflated with CORZ/CORZQ common stock.

cases.factual_findings: SEC-filed security data identifies Bit Brother CUSIP G1144D125 as new Class A ordinary shares. Issuer evidence later states its ordinary shares continued as BETSF after Nasdaq delisting.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The unusually long CUSIP chain reflects predecessor names, jurisdictional/recapitalization changes and reverse splits. It does not establish a non-common class in the canonical interval.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that the reviewed BETS/BETSF equity lineage was preferred, partnership/unit, trust, warrant or right.

cases.factual_findings: MedAvail Holdings CUSIP 58406B103 is expressly identified as common stock, $0.001 par value. Later evidence confirms the same CUSIP remained common stock.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: Other CUSIPs belong to predecessor/reorganization and reverse-split identity history. The MedAvail traded class in the canonical interval is common stock.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that MDVL/MDVLQ represented a preferred or unit/warrant class.

cases.factual_findings: Cleco Corporation CUSIP 12561W105 is expressly identified as Common Stock in an SEC Schedule 13G, covering the central identity in the canonical interval.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: Additional CUSIPs reflect predecessor/related identity records. They are retained as identity anomalies and do not make the Cleco public common-stock type ambiguous.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that the CNL/Cleco traded security in the interval was a preferred, unit, trust, warrant or right.

cases.factual_findings: SEC merger-related ownership reporting identifies GlobalSantaFe's outstanding security as ordinary shares, par value $0.01, and states each GlobalSantaFe ordinary share was converted in the 2007 Transocean merger.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: G3930E101 is the GlobalSantaFe security; G7805C108 is associated with the merger/successor chain. The legal type before merger was ordinary corporate equity.
cases.contradiction_search: GlobalSantaFe also had authority concerning preference shares, but no evidence shows ticker GSF represented a preference share; the merger documents explicitly describe the outstanding GSF shares as ordinary shares.

cases.factual_findings: Christopher & Banks Corporation CUSIP 171046105 is expressly identified as common stock, par value $0.01 per share. The later bankruptcy-style ticker suffix does not alter the earlier decision-period legal type.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP 105658108 is an identity-chain anomaly/related predecessor entry. The type of 171046105 itself is authoritative and unambiguous.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that the reviewed Christopher & Banks public security was a non-common instrument.

cases.factual_findings: SEC-filed records identify ATC Technology Corp ticker ATAC with CUSIP 00211W104; the predecessor Aftermarket Technology CUSIP 008318107 is identified as common stock. The corporate rename/identity lineage retained ordinary common equity.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: 00211W104 and 008318107 capture the ATC Technology/Aftermarket Technology identity transition; the anomaly is corporate identity/CUSIP continuity, not security-type ambiguity.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that ATAC represented preferred stock, units, warrants or rights during the canonical interval.

cases.factual_findings: SkillSoft's 2010 acquisition announcement states shareholders would receive cash for each SkillSoft ordinary share or ADS. Depositary program records identify CUSIP 830928107 as a sponsored ADR with a 1:1 ordinary-share-to-DR ratio and trace prior CUSIP 83170A206 to the same program lineage.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The CUSIP sequence reflects the SmartForce-to-SkillSoft name change and depositary-program history; the decision-period listed security was a depositary receipt on ordinary shares.
cases.contradiction_search: No evidence that SKIL represented preferred equity or another non-common underlying instrument.
